subject: Request: Offramp safeguard + staged credit amendment for Viora Health
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@viorahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17 14:23 -0700
Subject: draft amendment request: early off-ramp protections

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We discussed an initial 12-month commitment but the board is asking for an explicit off-ramp if volume materially decreases during the pilot. They asked for: a staged downsell credit if we scale back in months 4–12, a clear trigger definition for "material reduction," and a 90-day notice window.

Can Redwood provide language (amendment) that preserves our committed pricing for month 1–3, then gives a calibrated credit schedule thereafter? We prefer simple math (tiered % credit tied to committed throughput).

I attached a one-page summary of what they'd sign on (proposed-amendment-v1.pdf). If there are legal constraints, let us know.

Best,
Samira
--
Samira Khan
Director of Product, Viora Health
samira.khan@viorahealth.com

From: Viora Health Legal <legal@viorahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@viorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-17 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: draft amendment request: early off-ramp protections

Karthik,

Quick note from Legal: we redlined the vendor-friendly version to add clearer triggers and a remediation period. We also flagged the proposed credit schedule for review — the finance team wants two alternative schedules (credit bucket vs percentage-of-billed) so they can model downstream impact. We attached our redlines (viora-redlines.docx).

Key asks from our side:
- Specific trigger definition: e.g., sustained 40% throughput drop vs monthly baseline for 60 days.
- Maximum aggregate credit cap
- Single opt-out clause for early termination tied to a 90-day notice and payment of a one-time unwind fee

If Redwood has any standard playbooks for staged downsell/rollback protection and maximum credit buckets, please escalate internally — this will go to procurement.

Regards,
Viora Legal

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@viorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: draft amendment request: early off-ramp protections

Marissa / Laura,

Forwarding Viora's redlines and request. The asks are non-standard: staged downsell credits, defined triggers, and an opt-out/unwind fee. If we accept a percentage-based credit schedule with a cap, the estimated exposure (conservative) is ~ $220k over 12 months for the initial commit level they proposed.

Why I am escalating: the credit exposure exceeds standard deal-desk thresholds and the wording will set a precedent for later mid-market deals. I recommend we offer a structured 3-tier remediation schedule + a capped credit bucket and require 90-day notice + a one-time unwind fee (suggest $25k) to limit moral hazard.

Attached: proposed-amendment-v1.pdf and Viora's redlines.

Asks:
- Marissa: executive sign-off or alternate wording we can present to legal.
- Laura: any objections from a revenue ops perspective?

I can host a 30-min call with Viora Legal if you prefer.

Thanks,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18 14:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: draft amendment request: early off-ramp protections

Karthik — thanks for the tag. After reviewing the redlines and running a quick exposure calc with Finance, I approve the following guardrails (deal-desk approval):

1) Staged credit schedule (accepted):
   - Months 1–3: no credits (onboard period)
   - Months 4–6: up to 25% credit on marginal months where throughput < 70% of baseline
   - Months 7–12: up to 40% credit on marginal months where throughput < 50% of baseline
2) Aggregate credit cap: $200,000 for the first contract year
3) Trigger mechanics: sustained reduction defined as >40% decline vs baseline for any 60-day rolling window; baseline = average throughput of months 1–3
4) Opt-out/Unwind: 90-day written notice + one-time unwind fee $25,000; if the customer pays the unwind fee, credits cease as of termination date
5) Require DocuSign addendum that references the exact metrics and links to the monitoring dashboard; procurement must attest to acceptance of the trigger language

Conditions / Rationale: the cap controls downstream revenue risk; the unwind fee discourages opportunistic early exits; the staged schedule balances customer confidence with our unit economics.

I attached a short note for the contract team (deal-desk-approval-note.md) and prepared a DocuSign envelope — link is in the attachments (docusign-invite-link.txt).

Approve and proceed to legal markup with the above guardrails. If Viora insists on a higher cap, route back to Sales Leadership for an exec waiver.

- Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@viorahealth.com>, Viora Health Legal <legal@viorahealth.com>

Hi Samira / Viora Legal,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Marissa's approval, Redwood is prepared to move forward with the attached amendment that includes: the 3-tier staged credit schedule, $200k aggregate credit cap for year one, the 90-day notice and $25k unwind fee, and the trigger definition tied to months 1–3 baseline.

Action items:
- Viora Legal: please confirm in writing whether the redlines in viora-redlines.docx are acceptable with these guardrails.
- Samira: if procurement agrees, sign the DocuSign envelope (link included; contact me if you want it routed to a different signee).
- Contract team: Laura / Marissa — please prepare the final addendum and route to Legal for signature.

If Viora requests any expansion of the aggregate cap, we'll need an explicit executive waiver. Otherwise, we'll proceed under the approved terms.

Appreciate the coordination — will stand by for any edits.

Best,
Karthik
